scope: Targeted primary-source design review, not exhaustive systematic review

sources.title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models
sources.finding: Output interpretation in context and source support are distinct checks.
sources.limit: Contextual attribution is not legal approval.

sources.title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
sources.finding: Evidence sets and claim labels are both evaluated.
sources.limit: Wikipedia claims are not judicial reasoning.

sources.title: ContractNLI: A Dataset for Document-level Natural Language Inference for Contracts
sources.finding: Document entailment and evidence spans are separately annotated; exceptions remain difficult.
sources.limit: Contracts differ from speaker- and stage-sensitive judgments.

sources.title: RARR: Researching and Revising What Language Models Say, Using Language Models
sources.finding: Evidence research and minimal revision can improve attribution.
sources.limit: The paper notes downstream reasoning is not necessarily revised after factual edits; original method uses web search.

sources.title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
sources.finding: Factored verification hides the initial answer during individual verification.
sources.limit: Original verification uses model knowledge; gains do not establish independent legal evidence checking.

sources.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
sources.finding: Intrinsic correction is sensitive to oracle feedback, extra information and extra compute.
sources.limit: A finding for tested setups, not a universal impossibility theorem.

sources.title: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Key Condition Verification
sources.finding: Specific key-condition checking is a positive counterexample to generic reflection failure.
sources.limit: Short questions and mainly entity or numerical answers limit transfer to long judgments.

sources.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
sources.finding: Atomic fact support is assessed against a designated source.
sources.limit: Aggregate score error is not per-claim accuracy; disputed legal interpretations and coverage need separate treatment.

sources.title: Long-form factuality in large language models
sources.finding: Source checking decomposes facts, resolves context and uses bounded iterative search.
sources.limit: External search and length-based recall proxy differ from fixed legal sources and key-item coverage.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
sources.finding: Answer correctness and citation quality require separate evaluation.
sources.limit: Entailment-based evaluators have errors and do not solve complex legal chains.

sources.title: GEAR: Graph-based Evidence Aggregating and Reasoning for Fact Verification
sources.finding: Graph propagation aggregates multiple evidence statements.
sources.limit: FEVER gains are not proof of R-GCN legal benefits; do not adopt fully connected edges as factual links.

sources.title: DocInfer: Document-level Natural Language Inference using Optimal Evidence Selection
sources.finding: Document graphs address dispersed evidence and document entailment.
sources.limit: Do not import its extra architecture or reinforcement learning into this bounded project.

sources.title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning
sources.finding: Outcome-success-based labels and Best-of-N may mismeasure step correctness.
sources.limit: Mathematical verification findings motivate safeguards, not legal correctness guarantees.

sources.title: ProcessBench: Identifying Process Errors in Mathematical Reasoning
sources.finding: Evaluate error identification and correct-process retention separately.
sources.limit: Legal branches require local rather than global rejection after an error.

sources.title: Don’t Take the Premise for Granted: Mitigating Artifacts in Natural Language Inference
sources.finding: Hypothesis-only artifacts can yield nontrivial performance without premise understanding.
sources.limit: Evidence-sensitivity controls remain diagnostic, not natural legal supervision.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.finding: Relevant-information position affects tested long-context tasks.
sources.limit: Not a causal diagnosis of the current Qwen errors.

sources.title: The FACTS Grounding Leaderboard: Benchmarking LLMs’ Ability to Ground Responses to Long-Form Input
sources.finding: Groundedness must be paired with meaningful task completion.
sources.limit: Judge bias persists; multiple judges do not establish human legal gold.
